overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a posted meeting via two emails (a Chair update on May 28 and a member's site-visit report on September 8); no further relief was ordered because the emails were discussed publicly at later meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission deliberated outside a posted meeting via a May 28 email from the Chair to members correcting facts on pending applications; the Commission argued it contained only facts.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Chair Jernstrom’s email did not fit within any of the enumerated exemptions to the definition of deliberation and included updates on matters currently before the Board.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a member's September 8 email reporting his site visit to a parcel, sent to the other Commission members, was deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As this email reached more than a quorum of the Commission, and does not fit within the any of the exemptions to the definition of deliberation, we find that this email also constituted an impermissible deliberation outside of a posted meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Caution that a future similar violation determination may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Commission that a determination by our Office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
